notes: Hard single-focus reverse-engineering task: a compiled, source-free C target (/app/target/raycaster, built at image build time from an aux source removed from the image) renders a two-stage scene operation on a heightmap - a horizontal median-of-3 despike with clamped windows, then a west->east raycast shadow pass with slope-1 clearance falloff and STRICT comparison, emitting 'LIT <count>' plus a #/. mask. The agent must recover every semantic detail purely by probe grids and/or objdump/gdb (median window+clamping, ray direction, exact falloff, strict-vs-tie behavior, exact output bytes) and reimplement it in pure Python that matches byte-for-byte on hidden grids probing ties, descending-by-1 ramps, edge spikes, W=1/W=2 rows, 0/255 extremes, and 512-wide grids. Differs from calm-hearth's RE subtask (3x3 blur convolution, space-separated integer output): different operation class (morphological filter + ray march vs linear convolution), different output contract (mask art + summary line vs integer grid), and the reimplementation is pure-Python-only (no native invocation). Rubric total 15 -> hard; reasoning_depth 3 (two interacting passes + strictness corner), debugging_ambiguity 2 (multiple plausible models fit partial probes), quantitative_correctness 2 (byte-identical output).
